column2: Thousands of spectators cheered from the stands as the runners crossed the finish line.
column3: 數千名觀眾在看台上歡呼，跑者衝過終點線。
column5: spect 看 + ator：站在旁邊看的人

column2: Tourists were amazed by the splendor of the palace, with its golden halls and mirrors.
column3: 遊客們被宮殿的輝煌所震撼，那裡有金色大廳和鏡子。
column4: the splendor of the palace (宮殿的華麗)
column5: splendor 諧音「死本的」：金光閃閃華麗到讓人沒話說

column2: The poem has four stanzas, and each one ends with the same line.
column3: 這首詩有四節，每一節都以同一行結尾。
column5: stanza 諧音「史丹札」：詩篇史丹札成一小節

column2: One surprising statistic shows that half of the students walk to school.
column3: 有一項令人驚訝的統計數字顯示，一半的學生走路上學。
column4: a surprising statistic (驚人的統計數字)
column5: statist 統計 + ic：用來說明事實的一個數字

column2: The steward carried a tray of drinks across the deck of the ship.
column3: 服務員端著一盤飲料穿過船的甲板。
column4: a ship's steward (船上的服務員)
column5: steward 諧音「史都華」：史都華管家，替大家張羅一切

column2: The stewardess helped passengers find their seats and showed them how to wear life jackets.
column3: 空服員協助乘客找到座位，並示範如何穿救生衣。
column5: steward 管家 + ess 女性：女管家，機上服務女生

column2: We put winter coats into storage in the attic after the weather turned warm.
column3: 天氣變暖後，我們把冬季外套放進閣樓儲藏。
column5: store 儲存 + age：把東西存起來的狀態或地方

column2: The smell of sulfur filled the air near the hot spring and reminded us of rotten eggs.
column3: 溫泉附近瀰漫著硫磺味，讓我們想起臭雞蛋。
column4: a yellow powder of sulfur (黃色硫磺粉)
column5: sulfur 諧音「薩福」：臭雞蛋味的硫，一聞就知道

column2: Out of superstition, he never walks under a ladder or opens an umbrella indoors.
column3: 出於迷信，他從不走過梯子下，也不在室內撐傘。
column5: super 超出 + stition 站：站在科學之外的信念

column2: Travelers stopped at a tavern near the crossroads to eat stew and rest for the night.
column3: 旅人在十字路口附近的小客棧停下來，吃燉肉並過夜休息。
column5: tavern 諧音「他萬」：旅人到這家店，萬事都有人招待

column2: The bank teller counted the bills twice before handing the money to the customer.
column3: 銀行出納員把鈔票數了兩次，才把錢交給顧客。
column5: tell 說 + er：古時負責「數」並報告金額的人

column2: We stayed up late watching a thriller in which a stranger kept following the hero.
column3: 我們熬夜看了一部驚悚片，片中一名陌生人一直跟蹤主角。
column5: thrill 刺激 + er：讓你心跳加速的故事

column2: The prince waited in the great hall until the king invited him to sit on the throne.
column3: 王子在大殿中等候，直到國王邀他坐上王座。
column4: sit on the throne (登上王位)
column5: throne 諧音「揉肉」：坐上去後，國王可以任意命令

column2: She gave him a small gift as a token of thanks for his help.
column3: 她送他一份小禮物，作為感謝他幫忙的心意。
column4: a token of appreciation (感謝的象徵)
column5: token 諧音「透肯」：透過小東西肯定你的心意

column2: A torrent of angry emails poured in after the company announced higher prices.
column3: 公司宣布漲價後，大量憤怒的電子郵件如洪流般湧入。
column4: a torrent of words (連珠炮似的話)
column5: torrent 諧音「偷論特」：洪水一沖，什麼都被偷走

column2: Our school will host a basketball tournament this weekend with twelve teams.
column3: 我們學校這個週末將舉辦一場有十二支隊伍的籃球錦標賽。
column5: tourney 競技場 + ment：隊伍輪流較量的比賽

column2: In the play, a traitor opened the castle gate and let the enemy soldiers in.
column3: 劇中，一名叛徒打開城堡大門，讓敵軍士兵進來。
column4: a traitor to the country (叛國者)
column5: trai 像 trade 交換：拿朋友換好處的人

column2: The old treasury in the castle once held the kingdom's gold and silver.
column3: 城堡裡的舊庫房曾存放王國的金銀。
column5: treasure 寶物 + y：放寶物的地方

column2: The two countries signed a peace treaty to end years of fighting.
column3: 兩國簽署和平條約，結束多年的戰事。
column5: treat 對待 + y：雙方如何對待彼此的協議

column2: Students laid flowers by the statue as a tribute to the brave teacher.
column3: 學生們在雕像旁獻花，向那位勇敢的老師致敬。
column5: tribute 與 contribute 同源，獻出心意表達敬意

column2: We caught a trout in the cold mountain stream and grilled it over a fire.
column3: 我們在冰冷的山溪中捉到一條鱒魚，用火烤來吃。
column5: trout 諧音「吹勞特」：鱒魚在溪裡吹出水泡泡

column2: Mom opened a can of tuna and mixed it with mayonnaise for sandwiches.
column3: 媽媽打開一罐鮪魚，拌上美乃滋做三明治。
column4: a can of tuna (一罐鮪魚)
column5: tuna 諧音「土那」：土裡土氣罐頭裡的大魚

column2: As an undergraduate, he lived in a dorm and studied biology for four years.
column3: 身為大學生，他住在宿舍，主修生物學四年。
column5: under 在下 + graduate 畢業生：還沒畢業的人

column2: Her vanity showed when she spent an hour in front of the mirror before school.
column3: 她上學前在鏡子前花一小時，顯出了她的虛榮。
column4: hurt someone's vanity (傷到某人虛榮)
column5: van 空 + ity：空空的內在，只剩外表的驕傲

column2: Water vapor rose from the hot soup and fogged up his glasses.
column3: 水蒸氣從熱湯升起，讓他的眼鏡起霧。
column5: vapor 諧音「飛玻」：水變成氣，飛上去啦

column2: Thick vegetation covered the mountainside, hiding the old path from view.
column3: 濃密的草木覆蓋山坡，使舊小徑看不見。
column5: vegetable 蔬菜 + ation：成片長出的各種植物

column2: The nurse found a vein in his arm and gently inserted the needle.
column3: 護理師在他的手臂上找到一條靜脈，輕輕地插入針頭。
column4: a vein in the leaf (葉脈)
column5: vein 與 vain 同音，血管細細如樹葉脈絡

column2: The program asked each viewer to vote for a favorite song by text message.
column3: 節目請每位觀眾用簡訊投票選出最喜歡的歌曲。
column5: view 看 + er：看電視節目的人

column2: Despite his age, the old farmer worked with great vigor from sunrise to sunset.
column3: 儘管年紀大了，這位老農夫仍從日出到日落都充滿活力地工作。
column5: vigor 諧音「威格」：威風又格外有勁的活力

column2: Every good movie needs a villain who makes the hero's journey harder.
column3: 每部好電影都需要一個反派角色，讓主角的旅程更艱難。
column5: villain 諧音「微籃」：小小籃子裡藏著壞心眼的人

column2: Grapes grow on a vine that winds around a wooden frame in the garden.
column3: 葡萄長在園子裡纏繞著木架的藤蔓上。
column5: vine 諧音「萬」：萬條藤蔓纏滿牆

column2: The violinist closed her eyes and played so beautifully that the room fell silent.
column3: 小提琴手閉上眼睛，演奏得如此優美，整個房間都靜了下來。
column4: a talented violinist (有才華的小提琴手)
column5: violin 小提琴 + ist：拉小提琴的人

column2: The potter displayed fine ware at the market, from teacups to large clay jars.
column3: 陶工在市集展示精美的陶器，從茶杯到大陶罐都有。
column5: ware 與 wear 同音，擺出來的東西都是賣貨

column2: He poured a glass of whiskey and sat by the fire to read.
column3: 他倒了一杯威士忌，坐在火邊讀書。
column4: a glass of whiskey (一杯威士忌)
column5: whiskey 諧音「微斯基」：微微醉的飲料，大人專用

column2: Scotland is famous for its whisky, which is stored in oak barrels for many years.
column3: 蘇格蘭以威士忌聞名，這種酒要在橡木桶裡存放許多年。
column5: whisky 是蘇格蘭寫法，少一個 e，簡單一些

column2: The widower raised three children alone after his wife passed away.
column3: 這位鰥夫在妻子過世後獨自撫養三個孩子。
column5: widow 寡婦 + er 男性：喪妻的男人

column2: Hikers were lost in the wilderness for two days before rescuers found them.
column3: 健行者在荒野中迷路兩天，後來才被救援人員發現。
column4: survive in the wilderness (在荒野求生)
column5: wild 野 + erness：野生世界，沒有路沒有人

column2: Rangers protect the wildlife in the national park, from deer to tiny insects.
column3: 護管員保護國家公園內的野生生物，從鹿到小昆蟲都在內。
column5: wild 野生 + life 生命：野外的生命

column2: The farmers told a sad story of woe after the flood destroyed their crops.
column3: 洪水毀掉莊稼後，農夫們訴說著一段悲慘的苦難。
column4: a tale of woe (悲慘的遭遇)
column5: woe 諧音「喔」：遇上悲傷，只能嘆一聲「喔」

column2: A woodpecker drummed on the old oak, and the sound echoed through the forest.
column3: 一隻啄木鳥在老橡樹上敲擊，聲音在森林裡迴盪。
column4: a tapping woodpecker (啄木的啄木鳥)
column5: wood 木頭 + pecker 啄的鳥：專門啄木頭的鳥
